digest.component_or_area: store lock management and compaction sweep
propositions: When a compaction sweep holds the store write lock, a blocked session receives a LockTimeout naming only a bare pid without identifying the holder as a compaction process or stating whether interrupting it is safe.

The compaction sweep code already possesses the information needed to label lock holders with their operation type and interruptibility status, but this information does not reach error messages or operators.
A bare pid in a lock timeout error message causes operators to conservatively wait rather than safely interrupt a long-running, restartable compaction sweep, prolonging incidents.

The solution uses an ambient contextvars-based operation label that reaches lock owner stamps without modifying per-ticket acquisition call sites in compact_txn.py, preserving forward compatibility of the v2 lock stamp format.

The LockTimeout error message must render the operation label and append a remedy statement for known interruptible operations like compact-sweep, instructing operators that interruption is safe and the next trigger will re-fold.
An unlabelled lock holder must render identically to today's output, and staleness/reclamation logic must ignore the operation label to preserve existing lock reclamation behavior.
